variables.input: fetch metrics | filter metric.key == "airflow.ti.start" | summarize by:{dag_id} | fields dag_id | limit 500
fetch metrics | filter metric.key == "airflow.ti.start" and in(dag_id, $dag_id) | summarize by:{task_id} | fields task_id | limit 500

0.content:
# Airflow Per-DAG Drill-Down — Dynatrace Dashboard

Companion drill-down to `01-airflow-fleet-metrics.json`. Environment: Airflow 3.x, OTLP metrics+traces on (`otel_prefix="airflow"`), hybrid **CeleryExecutor + KubernetesExecutor**, **Edge workers** in use, **OpenLineage** enabled, ~200+ DAGs / high concurrency. Built with DQL tiles (Grail).

**Variables:** `dag_id` (multi-select, populated from `airflow.ti.start`) scopes every tile on this dashboard — for a true single-DAG drill-down, select exactly one value. `task_id` (multi-select, dependent on `dag_id`) additionally scopes the task-focused trend tiles in Section 2; it is intentionally **not** applied to the per-task breakdown tables (those are meant to show every task in the DAG at once) — leave it unselected unless you want to narrow a specific trend tile to one or a few tasks.

**Metrics-vs-traces reminder:** metrics never carry `run_id` — no tile here filters a metric by `run_id`. A true per-run view (this DAG's most recent run, or one specific `run_id`) requires trace data (`fetch spans`) and is intentionally left to the `03-airflow-dagrun-metrics-traces.json` dashboard, not duplicated here.

1.content:
## 1. DAG Run Overview

> All tiles filtered by the `dag_id` variable. `airflow.dagrun.*` metrics are documented as per-DAG timers/counters in the Airflow metrics reference; confirm on your OTLP pipeline that they arrive as a metric with a `dag_id` tag (rather than a per-DAG metric name suffix) before trusting the filter below.

2.title: DAG run duration — success vs failed (p50/p90/max)
2.subtitle: Run duration drift shows as a rising p50/p90; failure spikes show as failedMax jumps. Timer metric — requires OTLP exponential-histogram support for accurate percentiles.

3.title: Schedule delay
3.subtitle: Alert-worthy: sustained p90 above ~5 min (300s — tune to this DAG's schedule interval) suggests scheduler contention or a DAG scheduled too tightly.

4.title: Dependency-check duration (p90)
4.subtitle: REVIEW: prompt/spec name this `dagrun.dependency-check` (hyphen); Airflow's own metrics reference has historically documented it as a per-dag timer with the dag_id embedded in the metric name rather than a tag. Confirm the exact emitted key/tag shape on your version before trusting this filter.

5.title: First-task scheduling vs start delay (p90)
5.subtitle: A rising schedulingP90 with flat startP90 points to scheduler slowness; the reverse points to executor/worker capacity being the bottleneck for this DAG's first task.

6.title: Run success rate
6.query: timeseries success=count(airflow.dagrun.duration.success), failed=count(airflow.dagrun.duration.failed), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id) | fieldsAdd successRate = success / (success + failed) * 100
6.subtitle: Run counts derived from the duration timers (one sample per completed run); confirm this matches your definition of a completed run count.

8.content:
## 2. Task Breakdown Within This DAG

> All tiles filtered by `dag_id` and grouped/split by `task_id` to show every task in the DAG at once — the `task_id` variable is intentionally **not** applied here so the breakdown stays complete. At 200+ DAGs a single DAG can still have a large task count; tables below are sorted and top-N limited as a precaution.

9.title: Task successes vs failures by task_id (sorted by failures desc)
9.query: timeseries successes=sum(airflow.ti_successes), failures=sum(airflow.ti_failures), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id} | sort failures desc | limit 50

10.title: Task duration by task_id (p50/p90/p99)
10.query: timeseries p50=percentile(airflow.task.duration,50), p90=percentile(airflow.task.duration,90), p99=percentile(airflow.task.duration,99), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id} | sort p99 desc | limit 50
10.subtitle: Sorted by p99 desc to surface the tasks dominating this DAG's critical path. Timer metric — requires OTLP exponential-histogram support for accurate percentiles.

11.title: Selected task duration trend (p50/p90/p99)
11.query: timeseries p50=percentile(airflow.task.duration,50), p90=percentile(airflow.task.duration,90), p99=percentile(airflow.task.duration,99), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id) and in(task_id, $task_id)
11.subtitle: Populates once one or more task_id values are selected in the task_id variable; shows the time-trend view for the selected task(s) instead of the DAG-wide top-N snapshot.

12.title: Scheduled vs queued duration by task_id
12.query: timeseries schedP90=percentile(airflow.task.scheduled_duration,90), queuedP90=percentile(airflow.task.queued_duration,90), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id} | sort queuedP90 desc | limit 50
12.subtitle: scheduled_duration = waiting on the scheduler; queued_duration = waiting on executor/worker capacity. High queuedP90 with low schedP90 points at capacity, not the scheduler. Timer metrics — require OTLP exponential-histogram support.

13.title: Live task state board (scheduled / queued / running / deferred)
13.query: timeseries scheduled=avg(airflow.ti.scheduled), queued=avg(airflow.ti.queued), running=avg(airflow.ti.running), deferred=avg(airflow.ti.deferred), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id} | limit 50
13.subtitle: A stacked-bar rendering of this same query (state counts per task_id) works well as an alternate visualization in the Dynatrace UI if preferred over the table.

14.title: Recent task activity: start/finish by task_id and state
14.query: timeseries starts=sum(airflow.ti.start), finishes=sum(airflow.ti.finish), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id, state} | sort starts desc | limit 50

15.title: Task instances killed for missing heartbeats, by task_id
15.subtitle: Alert-worthy: any nonzero value indicates zombie task cleanup for this DAG.

16.title: Tasks killed externally, by task_id
16.subtitle: Alert-worthy: unexpected external kills often indicate OOM or manual intervention.

17.title: Previously-succeeded skips, by task_id
17.subtitle: REVIEW: `previously_succeeded` is listed in the Airflow metrics reference as a counter but its tag set isn't spelled out explicitly — confirm it actually carries dag_id/task_id tags on your version before trusting this filter/split.

18.content:
## 3. Task Lifecycle / DAG Structure Changes

> All tiles filtered by `dag_id`.

19.title: Tasks removed from / restored to DAG, by run_type

20.title: Task instances created, by run_type
20.subtitle: REVIEW: fleet dashboard split this metric by task_type; if your version tags it with both run_type and task_type, add task_type as a second by: dimension here.

21.title: DAG callback exceptions
21.subtitle: Alert-worthy: any nonzero value means a DAG-level callback (on_success/on_failure/etc.) raised an exception. REVIEW: confirm this metric carries a dag_id tag on your version (some Airflow metrics embed the dag_id in the name instead).

22.content:
## 4. Associated File-Processing Health

> These two metrics are **file/bundle-scoped, not dag_id-scoped** — Airflow does not tag them with dag_id. Tiles below filter by `file_name`/`bundle_name` matching this DAG's file instead of by the `dag_id` variable. **If this DAG shares its file/bundle with other DAGs (a common pattern at 200+ DAGs), these numbers reflect the whole file's parsing, not just this DAG** — confirm the file's DAG count before reading these as DAG-specific.

23.title: Last parse duration for this DAG's file
23.subtitle: REPLACE $this_dag_file_name with (or add a dashboard variable for) this DAG's actual file path, since Dynatrace has no dag_id tag to join through here.

24.title: Seconds since last successful parse for this DAG's file
24.subtitle: Alert-worthy: red if this DAG's file hasn't parsed successfully in >5 min (tune to your parse interval). Same file_name caveat as the tile to the left.

25.content:
## 5. Edge Worker Tasks For This DAG

> Edge workers are in use in this deployment, so this section is active. Filtered by `dag_id`; split by `queue`, `task_id`, `state`.

26.title: Edge worker task start/finish, by queue, task_id, state
26.query: timeseries starts=sum(airflow.edge_worker.ti.start), finishes=sum(airflow.edge_worker.ti.finish), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{queue, task_id, state} | sort starts desc | limit 50
26.subtitle: REVIEW: confirm `airflow.edge_worker.ti.start`/`.ti.finish` actually carry a dag_id tag on your version — the Airflow traces/metrics reference documents these primarily with worker_name/queue tags; dag_id tagging on edge-worker task events isn't explicitly spelled out and should be verified before relying on this filter.

27.content:
## Cardinality Notes

At 200+ DAGs with high concurrency, `dag_id × task_id` (and `dag_id × task_id × state`, used in Section 2's activity and state-board tiles) is the highest-cardinality combination used on this dashboard. Because every tile here is pre-scoped by the `dag_id` variable (ideally to a single DAG), cardinality is naturally bounded to that one DAG's task count rather than the fleet's — this dashboard is safe to use without additional pre-aggregation as long as `dag_id` is kept scoped to one (or a small handful of) DAGs. If a single DAG itself has an unusually large number of tasks (dynamic task mapping, hundreds of mapped task instances), keep the `limit` clauses in the breakdown tables and consider adding a `map_index` filter/variable to narrow further. Do not remove the `dag_id` variable's scoping role by leaving it unselected — an unscoped view here reproduces the fleet dashboard's cardinality risk without its pre-aggregation.
